Definition: from G2860; a diving-place, i.e. pond for bathing (or swimming):--pool.
BiblicalUsage: Kolymbethra is a pool, a place for bathing and swimming. John 5:2 names the pool of Bethesda at Jerusalem, with five porches, John 5:7 has the impotent man saying he has no man to put him into the pool when the water is troubled, and John 9:7 sends the blind man to wash in the pool of Siloam, and he came seeing.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the pools are where Jesus meets the helpless: the man with no one to put him in, and the blind man sent to wash. I hold that Bethesda and Siloam are the same lesson, that the water does nothing until the word of Jesus sends a man to it.
